title: Toy Car Inverse Graphics
summary: Recover the geometry of a customized miniature car, glazing, and draped display from five calibrated images.
taskPrompt: Reconstruct the customized miniature-car display shown in the five calibrated diagnostic images under `input/views/`. Recover the car body and trim, glazing, wheels, and the irregular draped fabric beneath it in the supplied world coordinate frame. The images depict the actual target geometry; a stock toy-car asset, even if visually similar, will not match its dimensions, panel profile, or fabric folds without modification. Read `input/RECONSTRUCTION_BRIEF.md` and `input/public_cameras.json` for the scale and camera contract. Submit a self-contained binary glTF at `output/reconstructed_scene.glb` and a short `output/reconstruction_report.md` describing your geometry construction and scale checks. Do not alter files under `input/`.
agentMustDo: Use all five calibrated views to align geometry in world coordinates.
Recover the customized front/rear body profile, wheels, glazing, and non-boxlike fabric folds.
Export real 3D mesh surfaces in a self-contained GLB, not camera-facing cards.
Write a concise report of modeling choices, scale checks, and remaining mismatch.

inputFiles.name: Five diagnostic views
inputFiles.description: Camera001, Camera002, Camera004, Camera006, and Camera007 of the customized scene.

inputFiles.name: Public camera calibration
inputFiles.description: Perspective intrinsics and camera-to-world transforms for the five views.

inputFiles.name: Reconstruction brief
inputFiles.description: Coordinate frame, approximate dimensions, component scope, and deliverables.

deliverables.description: Self-contained target reconstruction in the supplied world coordinates.
Brief modeling, scale, and limitation notes.

constraints: Do not replace geometry with billboards or view-dependent image planes.
The GLB must import into Blender without missing external files.
Mesh topology, object names, partitions, and materials are unrestricted.
Diagnostic colors distinguish parts; photorealistic material matching is not required.
evaluation: Geometry is imported in Blender and compared with a withheld complete scene. The score combines area-weighted symmetric surface distance, metric bounds, three held-out silhouettes, geometry validity, and report presence. Public-view-only cards, unmodified lookalike assets, missing components, extra geometry, and wrong scale lose credit.
